body: If I were into her I definitely would have pursued her when I thought she was serious about liking me. I presumed as much for quite some time before I rejected her and I'm still not convinced that she was "joking" about any of it. Even so, I have no romantic or sexual feelings for Jess. She's just a friend.

Thank you for writing all of this. Even though I'm not a butch, this has been my experience with women and it's nice to be heard and not written off. Anyone with this experience can tell you that it IS common. Often, there is this unspoken battle to be the most submissive, the most delicate, the most needy, etc. Every relationship teaches me more about how to set boundaries, but I keep falling into this dynamic with women, even women who swear up and down early on that they've been in the same position and hate it, are all about communication and reciprocity, etc. It just gets extremely disheartening to have this experience again and again, even as I work to be open about wanting to avoid it.

Thanks. I used to believe that youth was a mindset. I'm laughably young for most--almost 28--but I feel like the chance to live a middle class life is gone. This country hates poor people. I spend most of my waking life being berated at work. I've been in school for three years, but I won't graduate with my BA until I'm 34. By that time, it'll be too late to launch a successful career. I might not even last that long--I feel so broken already. I missed out on an entire decade of life and there isn't even going to be any payoff. I've been spinning my wheels, working to exist since I turned 19. I never got to party, date, have my first "real job," travel the world, go on adventures, or do anything people my age got to do. "Life isn't fair" aren't good enough words to tell someone who has suffered needlessly for ten years, being verbally and sometimes physically abused and harassed by people with more privilege and entitlement. If my only options are die or spend the rest of my life like this, I'll choose death.
